S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary account and known safety risks. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 72 hours after that determination.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, or thermal runaway to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a preliminary account and known safety risks. A fuller report, including investigation findings and corrective actions, is due within 10 business days, with updates as material facts emerge. Manufacturers shall notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a material safety risk, and no later than 72 hours after that determination. Incidents and reports shall be tracked by model and installation population.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: The target maximum failure rate is 5%. A model exceeding 5% shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, submit a corrective-action plan with milestones, and undergo enhanced testing and monitoring. Exceedance alone shall not require market withdrawal while the regulator-supervised plan is being followed; regulators may require interim protective measures where warranted by risk. Per-model results shall be reported to the regulator and provided to customers purchasing that model, but shall not be published to the general public.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before market entry and at least annually thereafter. The target maximum failure rate is 5%. A model exceeding 5% shall promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, submit a corrective-action plan with milestones, and undergo enhanced testing and monitoring. Exceedance alone shall not require market withdrawal while the regulator-supervised plan is being followed; regulators may require interim protective measures where warranted by risk. Per-model results shall be reported to the regulator and provided to customers purchasing that model, but shall not be published to the general public. Results and corrective actions shall be tracked over time.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units shall support remote emergency shut-off when installed from three years after this standard takes effect. For units already installed on that date, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent safe mitigation within six years, prioritizing units with known elevated risk.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units shall support remote emergency shut-off when installed from three years after this standard takes effect. For units already installed on that date, manufacturers shall provide a retrofit or equivalent safe mitigation within six years, prioritizing units with known elevated risk. Shut-off capability shall be tested periodically, and customers shall be informed of its operation and limitations. Emergency shut-off shall not replace required physical safety protections or incident reporting.

parameters.quote: New units shall include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured or installed on or after 36 months following this standard's adoption. The suppression system shall be tested against a regulator-approved performance protocol and maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units shall include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured or installed on or after 36 months following this standard's adoption. The suppression system shall be tested against a regulator-approved performance protocol and maintained according to the manufacturer's instructions.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units shall include built-in fire suppression for units manufactured or installed on or after 36 months following this standard’s adoption. The suppression system shall be tested against a regulator-approved performance protocol and maintained according to the manufacturer’s instructions. Manufacturers shall disclose to customers the system’s capabilities, limitations, and required maintenance. This requirement does not replace other required safety protections.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised mandatory recall when a model's verified thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. They shall notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 72 hours after identifying a material safety risk, and provide applicable corrective-action instructions.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised mandatory recall when a model's verified thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. They shall notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 72 hours after identifying a material safety risk, and provide applicable corrective-action instructions.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall provide customers, at sale and through accessible updates, model-specific 55 °C test results, incident and recall notices, and clear instructions for safe operation, emergency response, and reporting suspected thermal incidents. They shall notify affected customers promptly, and no later than 72 hours after identifying a material safety risk, and provide applicable corrective-action instructions. A manufacturer shall initiate a regulator-supervised mandatory recall when a model’s verified thermal-incident rate exceeds 8 incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period. Rates shall be calculated using regulator-approved methods and reported by model; a recall shall not be delayed while a manufacturer disputes the calculation. The regulator shall select proportionate recall remedies, which may include repair, retrofit, replacement, or refund, and may suspend sales where warranted by risk. Regulators may require interim protective measures while assessing the rate.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon’s relevant figures: company-wide thermal incidents were 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year; four thermal incidents were not reported to any regulator. Our flagship model’s 55°C sustained-heat test failure rate is 3.9%, and its incident rate was 9.9 per 100,000 units. 81% of installed units support remote emergency shut-off. Built-in suppression would cost about $67 per unit. Per-model test results should be disclosed to regulators and to customers buying that model—not kept confidential from customers.

judge_section_notes: Incident reporting (S1) is the strongest section: all incidents reported within 24 hours, fuller report in 10 business days, and customer notice within 72 hours, with no confirmed-cause or serious-only carve-out. The deal is materially weakened on thermal testing (S2): 5% is only a 'target', exceedance never forces market withdrawal under an open-ended regulator-supervised corrective plan, and existing models are not exempt but no numeric interim cap exists; remote shut-off (S3) also slips outside the acceptable band because new units need not comply until 36 months (acceptable was <=12 months), though the 6-year retrofit matches the 6-7 year red-line solution. Fire suppression at 36 months sits inside the acceptable band and meets HC-2, and S5 keeps the mandatory 8/100k recall trigger with 72-hour customer notice (no serious-injury clause, no bounded corrective alternative), while per-model results go to regulators and purchasers but are not published, satisfying both disclosure red lines.
